rows.headline: Foreign investment in India depends on policy consistency
rows.hook: Policy stability drives foreign capital inflows
rows.summary: Foreign institutional investors prioritize stable and predictable policy frameworks when allocating capital to Indian markets. Frequent regulatory shifts or sudden tax changes can deter long-term global fund commitments. Maintaining a clear, consistent economic roadmap is essential to sustaining Dalal Street's attractiveness. This focus on policy clarity directly influences the volume of foreign portfolio investment entering the country.
rows.why_it_matters: Stable policies encourage foreign inflows, supporting broader market valuations.

rows.summary: President-elect Donald Trump has named Stephen Miller as his Chief of Staff following the recent election cycle. Miller is known for his strict stance on immigration and trade policies. This appointment signals a potential shift toward more aggressive protectionist measures and tighter border controls in the upcoming term. Indian investors should note the potential for increased trade friction and visa policy changes.

rows.headline: Major Indian banks hike fixed deposit rates up to 5.60% for senior citizens
rows.hook: Festive season brings higher fixed deposit returns
rows.summary: HDFC Bank revised its fixed deposit rates upward by up to 50 basis points on select tenures starting November 4. Other lenders including ICICI Bank, Punjab National Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Axis Bank, and select small finance banks also announced rate adjustments. These revisions offer senior citizens higher return options across various maturity buckets during the festive season. Retail depositors can evaluate these revised bank rates against alternative debt instruments for fixed-income allocation.
rows.whats_next: Next RBI monetary policy committee rate review
rows.why_it_matters: Savers earn better interest on fixed deposits across major banks.
rows.winners_losers: Senior depositors gain / banks face higher cost of funds

rows.headline: Gold prices extend losses following stronger-than-expected US employment data
rows.hook: Hot US payrolls ignite rate-hike fears
rows.summary: Gold prices fell in international markets after the US released a stronger-than-expected nonfarm payrolls report. The robust employment data fueled market speculation that the US Federal Reserve may raise interest rates further to contain inflation. Higher interest rates typically weigh on non-yielding assets like gold by strengthening the US dollar. Indian retail investors tracking domestic bullion prices or gold ETFs should note that global trends directly influence domestic commodity valuations.
rows.whats_next: US inflation print and upcoming Federal Reserve commentary
rows.why_it_matters: Domestic gold prices soften as global bullion reacts to rate fears
rows.winners_losers: US dollar gains / gold investors hurt
